Article Title: 'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
Article Text:
Dhanush's strong pitch for Tamil

NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush has renewed the focus on the language debate with his remarks stressing the importance of learning Tamil and being "fluent in one's mother tongue."Speaking at an event, the actor strongly backed the Tamil language and urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue.Recalling his school days, Dhanush said, "When I was in school, we were fluent in Tamil and we struggled with English. Now the situation is opposite."He added, "Now, out of the 10 people I meet, eight don't know Tamil. One should be fluent in their mother tongue before everything else. To say I'm not fluent in Tamil is not a matter of pride. It's an insult. Focus on learning Tamil language."His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu, where the issue has frequently put the state government at odds with the Centre. Leaders across the state's political spectrum, from DMK chief and former CM MK Stalin to TVK founder and CM Vijay, have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.
Article Summary: Actor Dhanush has urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue. His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu. Leaders across the state's political spectrum have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.

Article Title: Bombay high court convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal
Article Text:
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday convicted former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal in the 2013 rape case filed by his former junior colleague, overturning his acquittal by a Goa trial court.The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa, where Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court had reserved its judgment last week after hearing arguments from both sides.Arguments on the quantum of sentence are currently underway, and the court is scheduled to pronounce its order on sentencing at around 2.30 pm.The Goa government had challenged Tejpal's acquittal after a sessions court cleared him of all charges in May 2021. The appeal was heard by Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar of the Bombay high court's Goa bench, which had directed Tejpal to remain present for the pronouncement of the verdict.Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had argued that the trial court committed a serious error by evaluating the complainant's conduct based on preconceived notions of how a survivor of sexual assault should behave.He submitted that there is no universal standard governing the reaction of a sexual assault survivor, as responses vary depending on an individual's education, personality, social background and circumstances.Tejpal, who was present in court, sought leniency, claiming that he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters.Mehta also argued that the trial court placed undue emphasis on minor inconsistencies in the complainant's statements instead of examining whether her core allegations remained consistent.Referring to an email sent by Tejpal to the complainant after the alleged incident, the Solicitor General argued that the accused had apologised for his "lapse of judgment", expressed shame and stated that he believed the encounter had been consensual. According to the prosecution, those statements amounted to an admission that an encounter had taken place.The defence, led by senior advocate Abad Ponda, argued that the prosecution had misread the apology emails as admissions of a sexual encounter.Ponda submitted that none of the emails contained any admission of a consensual physical or sexual encounter and that the references related only to a consensual verbal conversation of a sexual nature.The defence also questioned the complainant's credibility, arguing that her conduct before and after the alleged incident, along with emails, WhatsApp messages and documentary evidence, contradicted the prosecution's case.The high court's conviction reverses the trial court's acquittal, with sentencing to be decided after hearing arguments on the quantum of punishment.
Article Summary: The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa. Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court's conviction reverses the trial court's acquittal, with sentencing to be decided.

Article Title: Jharkhand protests: Five-member student panel to hold talks with Soren govt today - key points
Article Text:
The state government has repeatedly stressed its willingness to engage with the protesters.

Here are the top developments:

Students agree to talks, but seek public meeting

Government says doors are open

Probe gathers pace as arrests rise

NEW DELHI: Students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand have agreed in principle to hold talks with the state government, provided the discussions take place in the presence of the media. The development came even as the Crime Investigation Department (CID) arrested five more people in connection with the alleged recruitment scam, taking the investigation forward.Student leader Radhe Kumar said a five-member core committee would attend the meeting with government representatives. "Five members of our core team will attend the meeting. We will present our demands to the government through the SDO, who will convey them to the appropriate authorities. Once the government responds to our demands, we will decide our next course of action," he said.Student leaders said they were prepared to send a four- or five-member delegation for discussions after receiving a message from the government through the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO). However, they insisted that the talks should be transparent."We also had another demand: if the chief minister comes out to speak with us publicly in front of live media on an open platform, a proper resolution could be reached.In our previous protest, our representatives were taken into a closed room, and nothing came out of it. They are calling a five-member team just to stall and suppress our movement," one protester alleged.Another protester echoed the demand, saying, "The chief minister should listen to the students' demands in front of the press and media, and whatever promises he intends to fulfil should be stated publicly. For the last 26 years in Jharkhand, students' issues have been heard in closed rooms, and the files have remained closed forever."Student leader Ravindra Paswan said both sides had shown willingness to engage."The government has expressed its willingness to engage in dialogue, and we have also conveyed our willingness. Dialogue is essential in a democratic country as it is the only way to reach a resolution," Paswan said.He added that the students had placed two conditions before the government."Our primary condition is that the dialogue should take place directly with the chief minister, and we have been assured that the chief minister will be present. Secondly, we want at least two media representatives to be present during the discussions. The SDO has asked us to submit the names of our delegation members before 10 am, after which the date and time of the meeting will be communicated," he said.The state government has repeatedly stressed its willingness to engage with the protesters.Jharkhand minister Irfan Ansari said, "The chief minister has constituted the committee... We have opened the door for dialogue. Talks will take place, we will listen to your demands, and if they are reasonable, we will certainly accept them. They are our students, our children." He also accused the BJP of trying to politicise the issue.Rural development minister Deepika Pandey Singh said a committee had been formed and students had been asked to nominate their representatives so discussions could begin.However, Finance Minister Radhakrishna Kishore clarified that the ministers' group was only monitoring the agitation and was not a formal negotiation committee. He said the chief minister remained sensitive to the students' concerns and that the government was ready for talks whenever the students decided to engage.Earlier this week, chief minister Hemant Soren also said the government was open to dialogue and assured students that their demands would be considered seriously."...Many individuals have already been arrested and sent to jail, and investigative agencies are conducting raids at multiple locations. Overall, the agencies are working diligently and effectively on this matter, and I believe we will move forward towards a concrete resolution..." he said."The government's doors are open to everyone. Anyone who has demands can come forward and present their concerns. We are already aware of the issues to some extent, and if they present their views, the government will certainly consider them seriously," he added.The CID's latest action saw five more arrests in connection with the alleged examination irregularities, taking the total number of arrests to 19.The investigation is being led by an SIT, which is examining digital records, application logs and other evidence to establish the extent of the alleged recruitment irregularities.On August 5, Soren also met Governor Santosh Gangwar and briefed him on the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations as well as the ongoing protests. The Governor described the allegations as a serious matter and stressed the need for a transparent examination process to maintain the confidence of young job aspirants.According to an official release, Soren assured the Governor that the state government was committed to ensuring justice for students and that no injustice would be allowed.The protests began after the results of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination were declared on July 5. Aspirants have since been staging round-the-clock demonstrations and an indefinite sit-in, demanding cancellation of the preliminary examination and a review of recruitment tests conducted through TDPL agencies.
Article Summary: Students agree in principle to hold talks with the state government, provided the discussions take place in the presence of the media. The development came even as the Crime Investigation Department (CID) arrested five more people in connection with the alleged recruitment scam, taking the investigation forward.

Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to better prevent stalking-related crimes? Stricter laws against stalking Faster action on complaints More public awareness campaigns 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:
Ansari alleged that men associated with Abhijeet Dipke attacked him and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately.





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately. He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: ‘Miles to go before I sleep’: Omar gets poetic, says ‘wounds of Art 370 abrogation yet to heal’
Article Text:
All major political parties in Kashmir held protests and demonstrations, carrying banners and raising slogans describing Aug 5, 2019, as a ‘black day’

JAMMU: A row erupted after PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti was seen holding the Tricolour upside down during a candlelight protest over Article 370 on Tuesday evening. CM Omar Abdullah, however, played it down, saying he believed it was an inadvertent mistake rather than a deliberate act.“I cannot believe that a person who served as a CM would deliberately display the flag of the country upside down. It must be a mistake,” he said.

SRINAGAR/JAMMU: Striking a poetic note on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of the state of Jammu & Kashmir into two Union Territories, chief minister Omar Abdullah invoked celebrated American poet Robert Lee Frost as he said the wounds caused by the move had still not healed, and vowed that “the injustices done to us will be corrected”.“7 years, we haven’t forgotten & we haven’t reconciled far less accepted our current circumstances. My party & I remain committed to reversing all that was done to J&K that took away our rights & threatens our identity. ‘The woods are lovely, dark & deep. But I have promises to keep. And miles to go before I sleep’...” Omar said in a post on X, quoting from the poem ‘Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening’ by Frost, before he left for an inspection of flood-hit areas in Jammu’s Poonch district.Speaking to reporters in Poonch, the CM said, “The wounds of the abrogation are still there. We had hoped that at least some balm would be applied to those wounds and the promise of restoring statehood would be fulfilled...Seven years have passed, but the promise remains unfulfilled.”Barring BJP, which celebrated the abrogation of Article 370, all major political parties in Kashmir held protests and demonstrations, carrying banners and raising slogans describing Aug 5, 2019, as a ‘black day’.However, security forces foiled attempts by various parties to take out marches in Srinagar.Senior functionaries of governing NC and Congress remained absent from the protests held by their parties, which focused on seeking restoration of statehood. The PDP march was led by Iltija Mufti, who accused cops of manhandling her during Tuesday’s attempted protest.“It’s on this day we were caged like animals while a govt drunk on power stripped our state of its special status, flag, residuary powers and constitution. Our peaceful fight for it will continue till the day we get every bit of it back,” Iltija said.Lt governor Manoj Sinha, on the other hand, hailed the decision, saying it had “dismantled the terror ecosystem to a large extent, strengthened law and order, restored equal rights and created opportunities that allow families to rebuild their lives with confidence”. “The transformation we witness today in J&K is due to the historic changes of Aug 5, 2019. That day marked a constitutional correction and a new beginning for the UT,” he said.
Article Summary: All major political parties in Kashmir held protests and demonstrations, carrying banners and raising slogans describing Aug 5, 2019, as a ‘black day’ A row erupted after PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti was seen holding the Tricolour upside down during a candlelight protest over Article 370.

Article Title: Lok Sabha approves Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill without debate
Article Text:
Moved by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, the bill seeks to recognise digital and virtual records as admissible evidence in courts

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Wednesday passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill — replacing a British-era law — without discussion amid opposition protests and sloganeering on multiple issues, as members refused to heed the chair’s call to debate the legislation.The government accused the opposition of disrupting proceedings. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju accused Congress, Left parties and SP of being against Lord Ram and demanded they apologise to the nation. Referring to the opposition’s skit in Parliament, he said it had “saddened” the government and claimed these parties had opposed Ram temple construction by wearing black bands.Moved by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman , the bill seeks to align the law with contemporary digital banking practices by recognising digital and virtual records as admissible evidence in courts. Replacing the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891, it expands the definition of ‘bankers’ books’ to include records maintained in physical, digital, virtual, cloud-based or any other form.Protests disrupted Question Hour, forcing an adjournment till 2pm. The bill was passed by voice vote before the Lok Sabha was adjourned.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill without discussion. The bill seeks to align the law with contemporary digital banking practices by recognising digital and virtual records as admissible evidence in courts. It expands the definition of ‘bankers�’ books’ to include records maintained in physical, digital, virtual, cloud-based or any other form.

Article Title: Life's changed in J&K, Ladakh since Article 370, 35(A) repeal: PM Modi
Article Text:
PM says since repeal infrastructure has expanded and opportunities in education, healthcare and sports have grown

NEW DELHI: The lives of the people of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh have witnessed wide-ranging transformation since Articles 370 and 35(A) were repealed, PM Narendra Modi said on the seventh anniversary of the decision, stating that the removal of the erstwhile state's special status marked a decisive new chapter for the region, now divided into two Union territories (UTs).Modi emphasised the special significance of the anniversary as his govt is commemorating the 125th birth anniversary of BJP's ideological inspiration Syama Prasad Mookerjee this year. Mookerjee had launched an agitation against Article 370 and died in incarceration in Jammu and Kashmir in 1953 after being arrested for entering it without the required permit."His lifelong commitment to national unity continues to inspire generations. What he envisioned decades ago found historic fulfilment on 5th Aug, 2019," PMModi said."Since then, infrastructure has expanded and opportunities in areas such as education, healthcare, entrepreneurship and sports have grown," he said. "Be it women or the marginalised communities, those who were denied their basic constitutional rights for decades have been empowered thanks to the full application of the Constitution of India," he said.Defence minister Rajnath Singh said a new era of peace, progress and equal opportunity has dawned for Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh have witnessed wide-ranging transformation since repeal, PM Narendra Modi says. PM says removal of erstwhile state's special status marked a decisive new chapter for the region, now divided into two Union territories (UTs)

Article Title: Government orders blocking of 7,393 links involved in film pirac
Article Text:
This was disclosed in a written reply by minister of state for information and broadcasting, L Murugan, to a question on the circulation of pirated films (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: The government has directed online intermediaries to block 7,393 links involved in film piracy, including 4,996 Telegram channels and 1,263 websites, the information and broadcasting ministry told the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.This was disclosed in a written reply by minister of state for information and broadcasting, L Murugan, to a question on the circulation of pirated films, OTT shows and other audiovisual content through Telegram and similar platforms.The government said it had strengthened the legal framework against online film piracy through amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023.
Article Summary: The government has directed online intermediaries to block 7,393 links involved in film piracy. This was disclosed in a written reply by minister of state for information and broadcasting, L Murugan. The government said it had strengthened the legal framework against online film piracy through amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023.

Article Title: Terrorist hideout busted in Poonch, ammo seized; search ops launched in Jammu, Kathua
Article Text:
Joint teams carried out cordon-and-search operations based on intelligence inputs about suspicious activity

JAMMU: Security forces busted a terrorist hideout in a remote village in J&K’s Poonch district, while joint teams carried out cordon-and-search operations in Jammu’s Akhnoor sector and Kathua’s Hiranagar sector based on intelligence inputs about suspicious activity, officials said Wednesday.Officials said the hideout, set up in a cave, was unearthed during a joint search operation by the Army’s Rashtriya Rifles and J&K Police in Bhoriwala dhok of Surankote tehsil on Wednesday morning. Troops seized two magazines of an AK assault rifle, 117 rounds of ammunition, and 17 rounds of 9mm pistol ammunition from the spot.Around 2pm Tuesday, a suspected Pakistani drone allegedly entered Indian airspace and was spotted hovering over the forward villages of Shukhmal, Devindera and Tapan in Bobiyan area of Kathua’s Hiranagar sector. BSF personnel tried to shoot it down, but the UAV, flying at a high altitude, managed to return across the border. A subsequent search of the area did not yield anything suspicious, officials said.A joint team of CRPF and J&K Police conducted another search operation from Parshuram Temple to Jandi Nallah in Hiranagar as part of an area-domination exercise.Separately, the Army and J&K Police launched a combing operation in Sunail Panchayat area of Jammu’s Akhnoor sector after a resident reported suspicious movement Tuesday.Meanwhile, separate cordon-and-search operations launched Tuesday in two locations in J&K’s Poonch district continued without any sighting or contact with terror suspects allegedly present in the area. Three suspects were allegedly seen near Gujjar Naar area, and four more were spotted close to Kherowali dhok in the remote Dhara Sangla village in Surankote sector.
Article Summary: Security forces busted a terrorist hideout in a remote village in J&K’s Poonch district. Troops seized two magazines of an AK assault rifle, 117 rounds of ammunition, and 17 rounds of 9mm pistol ammunition from the spot. Separately, a suspected Pakistani drone allegedly entered Indian airspace and was spotted hovering over the forward villages of Shukhmal, Devindera and Tapan.

Article Title: Unelected Bihar minister Deepak Prakash nominated as MLC days after SC questions cabinet continuance
Article Text:
Bihar minister Deepak Prakash (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bihar minister Deepak Prakash was on Tuesday nominated to the state Legislative Council, days after the Supreme Court questioned his continuance in the cabinet without being a legislator.According to a gazette notification, governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd.) nominated Prakash to the vacant seat left by BJP MLC Devesh Kumar's resignation.Prakash was first inducted into the then Nitish Kumar-led Bihar cabinet in November last year and was recently re-inducted into the BJP-led government headed by Samrat Choudhary. On both occasions, he was not a member of either House of the state legislature.His father, Upendra Kushwaha, whose Rashtriya Lok Morcha is a constituent of the BJP-led ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), thanked the BJP leadership but insisted the nomination was unrelated to the court proceedings.“I express my gratitude towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin. We shall work to take Bihar forward," Kushwaha told reporters, according to PTI."People file petitions for all sorts of things. When Deepak Prakash had first become a minister, the NDA had in principle decided that he would be sent to the Legislative Council in due course," he added.BJP sources, however, admitted Kumar had "sacrificed" his seat to accommodate Prakash. Kumar, whose tenure had less than a year left, resigned on July 31, saying it was a "voluntary decision".Last week, while hearing a petition challenging Prakash's continuance as minister, the Supreme Court raised the "legal question" of "how long can you have an unelected minister".Under constitutional rules, a person appointed as a minister must become a member of either House of the legislature within six months.
Article Summary: Bihar minister Deepak Prakash was on Tuesday nominated to the state Legislative Council. The Supreme Court questioned his continuance in the cabinet without being a legislator. His father, Upendra Kushwaha, thanked the BJP leadership but insisted the nomination was unrelated to court proceedings.

Article Title: With all eyes on delimitation & FCRA, Parliament monsoon session sinks deeper into deadlock
Article Text:
LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi led march demanding Union home minister Amit Shah's statement on alleged police excesses.

Opposition marches to Parliament

No special session

Rahul-Rijiju meet

Derek blames govt disruption

Bill on Supreme Court judges passed

NEW DELHI: Parliament remained paralysed for the 13th consecutive day on Wednesday as relentless protests by Opposition parties forced repeated adjournments in both Houses, even as the government pushed through key legislative business.Amid the deadlock, efforts to break the impasse gathered pace with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju holding meetings with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Union home minister Amit Shah , while Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately met BJP MPs over breakfast.Opposition MPs led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra marched from Prerna Sthal to Makar Dwar, demanding accountability from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against CJP protesters on July 20.They also raised the alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement issue and other matters. Priyanka Gandhi said those responsible for ordering the alleged use of pellet guns, tear gas and lathi charges against students must be held accountable, asserting that "This is a democracy, not a dictatorship; it is not someone's royal court."Rijiju dismissed speculation that the Monsoon Session could be extended or that a special session might be convened later this month.He said there was no proposal before the government to either prolong the current session or hold a separate sitting in mid-August.His clarification came amid continued disruptions that have prevented the Lok Sabha from completing Question Hour since the session began on July 20.Despite the logjam, the Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, by voice vote without discussion after Opposition members refused to end their protest.Rijiju accused Opposition parties of deliberately stalling the House despite time being allotted for debate. He also criticised the Congress, CPI and Samajwadi Party over their protests relating to the alleged Ram Temple donation theft, alleging they had disrespected Lord Ram through demonstrations inside the Parliament complex.In a significant political development, Rijiju met Rahul Gandhi in his Parliament office for nearly 50 minutes in what sources described as a confidence-building exercise aimed at ending the parliamentary deadlock. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was present throughout the meeting, while Gaurav Gogoi and K C Venugopal joined later.According to sources, discussions covered the proposed Delimitation Bill, the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) Bill and other contentious issues that have fuelled the ongoing standoff. It was Rijiju's second meeting with Rahul Gandhi in the past 10 days, signalling continued backchannel engagement between the government and the Opposition despite the public confrontation inside Parliament.Soon after meeting Rahul Gandhi, Rijiju met Amit Shah at Parliament House. Sources said the government is preparing to engage the Opposition on the proposed FCRA Bill and Shah is expected to address the issue in Parliament.Rijiju is also expected to reach out to leaders of other Opposition parties, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, in an effort to build consensus and restore normal functioning of the House. The proposed FCRA amendments have emerged as one of the key flashpoints of the session alongside the protests over NEET, police action against students and the Ram Temple donation controversy.Trinamool Congress leader Derek O'Brien accused the government of being responsible for the continued disruption in Parliament, alleging that Amit Shah's prolonged absence from the House had worsened the situation. O'Brien maintained that Opposition MPs continued to perform their parliamentary duties despite the protests by raising public issues through Zero Hour notices and starred questions.He highlighted his own notices seeking national recognition of the 75th anniversary of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity and raising concerns over the proposed FCRA Bill. TMC sources said the party had submitted more than 100 questions during the session on issues ranging from MGNREGA dues and manual scavenging to air pollution, bank frauds, the UDAN scheme and the Nirbhaya Fund.Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his official residence as part of his regular outreach during Parliament sessions. The gathering included MPs associated with the NDA as well as former AAP leaders who later joined the BJP. Senior BJP leaders Tarun Chugh, Vinod Tawde and party chief Nitin Nabin also attended.Sources told news agency PTI said the Prime Minister shared personal experiences and discussed governance, parliamentary strategy and constituency feedback with the MPs. The interaction forms part of Modi's practice of meeting smaller groups of BJP parliamentarians during every session to strengthen coordination and receive direct feedback from lawmakers.Despite the disruptions, the Rajya Sabha passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, completing Parliament's approval of the legislation. The Bill raises the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.Replying to the debate, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the increase was a "demand of the time" given the growing workload, rising pendency and the need for more Constitution Benches.He said the expansion would improve disposal rates and help ensure quicker access to justice. Meghwal also highlighted the government's ongoing investment in expanding Supreme Court infrastructure and reiterated its commitment to judicial reforms and the independence of the judiciary.
Article Summary: Parliament remained paralysed for the 13th consecutive day on Wednesday as relentless protests by Opposition parties forced repeated adjournments in both Houses. Despite the logjam, the Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, by voice vote without discussion. Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his official residence.

The unrest resulted in four fatalities and injuries to several others. In the document, a sharp demographic shift is observed.Highlighting major demographic shifts in Sambhal, the report notes that the Hindu population declined from 45 percent at the time of Independence to 15 percent currently, while Muslims now constitute 85 percent of the population.Speaking at the inauguration and foundation-laying ceremony for various development projects in Sambhal, the UP CM asserted that the state is transitioning from "appeasement" to "satisfaction," leaving no room for any demographic shift. Adityanath linked the violence to a history of “targeted actions” against Hindus under previous state governments.“The judicial commission submitted its report on the Sambhal incident on Thursday, revealing parts of how a conspiracy for riot unfolded in 2024," CM Adityanath said.According to the PTI, the panel traces Sambhal's history of communal strife to a 1953 Shia-Sunni clash, with major riots occurring in 1956, 1959, 1962, when Jan Sangh MLA Mahesh Gupta was stabbed, 1966, and 1976, when a mosque committee dispute and the murder of a maulvi triggered temple attacks and curfews.

An Indian tanker came under attack as it capsized after being hit by a projectile.Visual after the hit, shared by Press TV, shows massive fire engulfing the India-flagged cargo vessel in the Red Sea before the ship sank off Yemen’s western coast.The MSV Faize Noore Oliya was struck by a projectile in Yemeni waters on August 4, causing the vessel to catch fire before it sank near the port city of Hodeidah.The vessel was carrying 14 crew members, including 13 Indians and one Yemeni sailor. Senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also attended the meeting, which focused on the ongoing impasse in Parliament and the proposed Delimitation Bill.According to ANI sources, Rijiju sought to know the opposition's stand on the Delimitation Bill during the discussions.There is no move at present to introduce either the Delimitation Bill or the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill in a special Parliament session after Independence Day, government sources told PTI.
