Using the ruling party's Abusive warriors, they spread defamation against me claiming that I used unnecessary words during the Thanjavur protest. They registered false cases, thinking they could harass me by dragging me from Chennai to Thanjavur, and tried to satisfy someone," he said."Even after arresting me, I looked at the media and said that I view this arrest as a comedy, and only then came along. I did not run away in fear after seeing the police," he added.Udhayanidhi also referred to the Karur stampede in which 41 people died, accusing the chief minister of avoiding accountability."The whole country knows that today's Chief Minister, even when 41 people died in Karur, without meeting their families and without facing the media, fled head over heels in fear that he might be arrested.""Even after so many lives were lost in Karur - this is the same person who went to Malaysia within the next one month for a film promotion and danced around. The Chief Minister may fear arrest if he wants. I am not afraid of any of that," he said.The DMK leader also thanked party workers, alliance partners and other political leaders who condemned his arrest and participated in protests demanding his release."I express my gratitude to the leaders of various political parties, including friendly movements, who condemned my arrest, and to the party comrades across Tamil Nadu who showed unity in support of me," he said.
Article Summary: Udhayanidhi was briefly arrested on Tuesday morning, a day after his remarks during a protest in Thanjavur over the Cauvery water dispute with Karnataka sparked a political controversy. The ruling TVK alleged that his response carried a vulgar double meaning and accused him of lowering the standards of political discourse and insulting the dignity of women.

Article Title: 'Biggest attack since World War II': What stopped massive US strike on Iran? Trump reveals
Article Text:
Trump maintained that while he remains open to diplomacy

US President Donald Trump said that the United States was on the verge of launching what he described as the "biggest attack since World War II" on Iran before Tehran reached out to seek talks. He claimed that the prospect of a massive military strike pushed Iran back to the negotiating table.Speaking at an event in Las Vegas on Wednesday, Trump said Iranian officials contacted him just before the planned operation. "They called me and they said, 'Please don't do it, let's talk,'" Trump told supporters, presenting the outreach as a result of sustained US military pressure.Trump maintained that while he remains open to diplomacy, Washington's position on Iran's nuclear ambitions has not changed. "I'd rather make a deal because I don't want to kill people," he said. "But Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon."His remarks came as the Trump administration signalled that negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz were nearing a breakthrough. Trump said on Tuesday that "a lot of progress" had been made and suggested an agreement could be announced "tomorrow or the next day".Iran also indicated that talks were advancing. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran and Oman were in the "final stage" of drafting an agreement on the strategically vital waterway and that a joint statement could follow if "certain parties do not obstruct this process".According to regional officials cited by the Associated Press, Iranian and Omani negotiators have finalised a draft agreement and are awaiting approval from Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. The proposed deal is reportedly intended as a temporary arrangement that could pave the way for renewed US-Iran nuclear negotiations.However, major differences remain. Iran has insisted on retaining a degree of control over the Strait of Hormuz, while the US has rejected any agreement that would allow Tehran to charge transit fees or strengthen its hold over one of the world's most important energy corridors.The waterway has remained at the centre of the conflict since the war began on February 28, with disruptions to shipping sending oil prices higher and putting pressure on the global economy. Around a fifth of the world's traded oil and natural gas previously passed through the strait.Despite the diplomatic momentum, tensions across the region remain high. Iranian-backed Houthi rebels claimed fresh missile attacks on Saudi-linked shipping in the Red Sea, while fighting also threatened to flare again along the Israel-Lebanon border.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said the United States was on the verge of launching what he described as the "biggest attack since World War II" on Iran. He claimed that the prospect of a massive military strike pushed Iran back to the negotiating table. His remarks came as the Trump administration signalled that negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz were nearing a breakthrough.

Article Title: Nagpur rape accused planned teen’s captivity, wants pizza, soft bedding & VIP comfort in police lock-up
Article Text:
A 20-year-old BBA student faces abduction and sexual assault charges. He is demanding luxury amenities and refusing police questioning.





NAGPUR: The 20-year-old BBA student, arrested in the alleged abduction and sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl, has begun complaining about dingy walls and a stinking toilet in lock-up and demanded pizza for breakfast and premium food for dinner. He is also refusing custodial interrogation after his top lawyer alleged police highhandedness in court on Tuesday, leaving cops in a fix.The accused, who refused medical examination and treatment, also refused to share his cell phone password and the survivor’s mobile, which he took control of during her 24-hour captivity. Sources at Hudkeshwar police station said the youth has been deftly stonewalling queries even as cops struggled to gather digital evidence. He was forcibly taken for medical examination on Tuesday.“The accused has been keeping the lock-up staff on their toes with repeated demands for VIP treatment. He has also been grumbling about sleepless nights, mosquito bites and demanded a thick cushion or a soft bedding and immediate installation of insect repellents in the lock-up,” said a senior official.Police sources said the accused has also been arguing with officers round the clock and has been pinning the blame on the 16-year-old girl for his sexual exploits.On Tuesday, the accused had levelled serious allegations against police before the special judge, alleging that police stole Rs 70,000 in cash from his rented flat, thrashed him and refused to return his spectacles and shoes. Police officers told TOI the youth is trying to inflict injuries on himself to strengthen the false narrative.Senior inspector Anamika Mirzapure of Hudkeshwar police station stated they have cooperated with the accused and met his basic needs. “If any accused demands luxury, soft beds, better food, and constantly argues, we cannot help. The accused is stalling interrogations and refusing to cooperate. We are constantly counselling him,” she said. Hassled policemen are monitoring him to prevent any self-harm attempts while continuing efforts to extract information.
Article Summary: BBA student arrested in alleged abduction and sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl. He has demanded pizza for breakfast and premium food for dinner. He is refusing custodial interrogation after his top lawyer alleged police highhandedness in court on Tuesday.

Article Title: 'Very difficult to communicate': Iran President Pezeshkian on Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei
Article Text:
Pezeshkian says it is "very difficult" to communicate Mojtaba Khamenei

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that communicating with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is "very difficult", as the latter continues to remain out of public view after succeeding his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, following his death.Pezeshkian's remarks came after US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz was likely to reopen in a day or two.Mojtaba Khamenei was also reportedly wounded in the strikes that killed the longest-serving Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Trump has repeatedly claimed that the new Supreme Leader is in "bad shape"."It is very difficult to communicate with him at the moment, but in any case, his presence is a very great source of strength for us so that we can continue," Pezeshkian said.While Mojtaba Khamenei has continued to issue written statements, his absence from public view during Iran's conflict with the United States has fuelled speculation about his ties with other senior officials.He notably did not appear at his father's funeral ceremonies last month.Pezeshkian, however, defended the Supreme Leader, saying he had held productive meetings with him and had been met with "kindness and very sound logic"."Unfortunately, the current situation allows some malicious people to describe him differently and to present a different image of him," he said.However, recent reports suggest that Pezeshkian is at odds with Mojtaba Khamenei, with the Supreme Leader reportedly issuing a "final ultimatum" that "any future resignation will be accepted."
Article Summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is "very difficult" to communicate with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The latter continues to remain out of public view after succeeding his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, following his death. Trump has repeatedly claimed the new Supreme Leader is in "bad shape"

Article Title: 2024 Sambhal violence: Panel traces communal clashes back to 1930s, calls town among UP's most sensitive
Article Text:
Following a court-ordered survey, a judicial commission delved into the violence in Sambhal





LUCKNOW: A substantial portion of the report, tabled by the judicial commission constituted by the Uttar Pradesh govt to probe Sambhal violence in 2024, focuses on Sambhal’s history and the disputed mosque site.The commission noted that Sambhal has long been regarded as a religiously significant town and is associated in Hindu tradition with Kalki, the future incarnation of Lord Vishnu.The report cites historical records and gazetteers describing the existence of the Harihar Mandir at the site where the Shahi Jama Masjid now stands.Referring to historical records, the commission said that the mosque is believed to have been constructed in 1526 during Babur’s reign and is a centrally protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).The structure has enjoyed protected status since 1920 under heritage conservation laws.The report said that ASI officials faced resistance during an inspection conducted in June 2024 and alleged that certain structural modifications had been made to the monument over time.The commission clarified that the question of whether the mosque was constructed over the ruins of a temple remains the subject matter of the pending civil suit and that no findings were recorded on that issue.The commission traced multiple episodes of communal violence in Sambhal from the 1930s onwards, including riots in 1947, 1948, 1958, 1962, 1976, 1978, 1980, 1986, 1990, 1992, 1995 and during the anti-CAA protests in 2019.According to the report, Sambhal has repeatedly witnessed Hindu-Muslim clashes and periodic communal unrest, making it one of the most sensitive towns in UP from a law-and-order perspective.The report referred to long-standing rivalries among influential Muslim groups and political factions in the district, which it said contributed to local tensions.Conducting one of the most extensive inquiries, the commission visited Sambhal shortly after the violence, inspected Jama Masjid and surrounding areas and held multiple rounds of hearings in Lucknow, Sambhal and through video conferencing.In all, 199 witnesses were examined, including 29 police personnel, 12 administrative officials, 19 medical professionals, 34 civilian witnesses, 78 detainees linked to the violence, media personnel, members of the Jama Masjid management committee, complainants, forensic experts and political figures.The commission reviewed FIRs, medical reports, postmortem records, forensic reports, ballistic evidence, CCTV footage, media recordings, drone footage and affidavits submitted by witnesses.According to the report, the controversy began on Nov 19, 2024, when Hari Shankar Jain and seven others filed original suit before the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandausi.The same day, the court allowed an application seeking appointment of an advocate commissioner to conduct a survey of the disputed site and directed that photography and videography be undertaken during the exercise.Advocate Ramesh Chandra Raghav was appointed survey commissioner and approached the Sambhal district administration for security arrangements.The first phase of the survey began on Nov 19 but could not be completed that day because of fading daylight and growing opposition from local political figures and supporters.The report said that when the remaining survey was conducted on Nov 24, thousands gathered around the mosque to oppose the exercise.Police and administrative officers repeatedly informed the crowd that the survey was being conducted under court orders, but tensions escalated. Stone pelting, arson and firing broke out, leading to clashes with security personnel.Police responded with tear gas shells, chilli grenades, rubber bullets, pump-action guns and other crowd-control measures.The violence left four people dead and several police personnel injured.The state govt constituted a judicial commission comprising Justice (retd) Devendra Kumar Arora as chairman, retired IAS officer Amit Mohan Prasad and retired DGP Arvind Kumar Jain as members.
Article Summary: Sambhal has long been regarded as a religiously significant town. The mosque is believed to have been constructed in 1526 during Babur’s reign. It is a centrally protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) The structure has enjoyed protected status since 1920 under heritage conservation laws.

Article Title: Mexican TikTok influencer Cesar Gastelum is shot dead during a livestream in Culiacan Sinaloa
Article Text:
Image Via Instagram

Cesar Gastelum is shot during TikTok livestream in Culiacan

TikTok star Gastelum becomes latest influencer killed during livestream

“real strawberry date.”

Mexican TikTok influencer Cesar Gastelum was shot and killed while livestreaming in Culiacan, Sinaloa, according to local authorities and reports. The 23-year-old creator was reportedly with friends outside a fast-food business when two people on a motorcycle approached the group. A recording of the livestream reviewed by Reuters reportedly showed the person riding the motorcycle firing a gun at Gastelum. The TikTok star had nearly 600,000 followers and was known for making funny videos. No arrests have been confirmed at the time of writing, while authorities continue to look into the shooting.The shooting happened in Culiacan, the capital and largest city of Sinaloa in northwestern Mexico. Gastelum was with a group of friends when two people on a motorcycle reportedly came toward them.According to Reuters, footage from Gastelum’s livestream appeared to show the motorcycle driver firing a gun at the influencer. The attack happened while he was broadcasting to his followers.A security official in Sinaloa confirmed that Gastelum had died following the shooting. He was 23 years old.Gastelum had built a large audience on TikTok, with almost 600,000 followers.He was mainly known for comedy and entertainment content and regularly shared videos with his audience.The shooting has shocked viewers because it happened while Gastelum was live on social media. His followers were able to see part of the incident through the livestream.At the time of writing, authorities have not confirmed any arrests connected to the killing. The reason for the attack has also not been publicly confirmed.Gastelum's death comes as another tragic case involving a Mexican social media creator being killed while broadcasting live.The incident has drawn attention because livestreams allow people to share moments with large audiences as they happen. In Gastelum's case, his final moments were connected to a broadcast that he was making for his followers.His most recent TikTok post was shared three days before his death. In the video, Gastelum appeared alongside another influencer named La Beba, who was wearing a red dress. Gastelum described the post as aCuliacan has also faced serious violence linked to conflicts between organized crime groups. The city has seen repeated security operations as authorities try to control violence in the area.However, officials have not said that Gastelum's killing was connected to organized crime, and no motive has been confirmed.
Article Summary: TikTok influencer Cesar Gastelum was shot and killed while livestreaming in Culiacan, Sinaloa, according to local authorities and reports. The 23-year-old creator was reportedly with friends outside a fast-food business when two people on a motorcycle approached the group. The TikTok star had nearly 600,000 followers and was known for making funny videos. No arrests have been confirmed at the time of writing.

Article Title: Bhiwandi crash: Buiding owner, repairs contractor booked; state orders probe
Article Text:
A five-storey Bhiwandi building collapsed, killing ten people and injuring three others

Hundreds of dangerous buildings in MMR, thousands at risk (Photo credit: Santosh Gupta)





MUMBAI: The state govt ordered an inquiry into the crash of a part of a five-storey Bhiwandi building that claimed 10 lives.An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) of BNS and relevant provisions of Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act for illegal construction, said DCP (zone 2), Thane, Pawan Basod.The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed and the CM Rs 5 lakh each.This was the third such major building collapse in Bhiwandi since 2020.Repairs began four days earlier after residents flagged falling plaster chunks and hired a contractor on their own. The building was not vacated during the work.Around 8pm on Thursday, residents noticed that a supporting pillar in wing B had developed a crack and was tilting, alerted the contractor and vacated the building.Workers were immediately brought in and the pillar was reinforced with iron support rods. Assuming that the structure had been stabilised, many residents went back into the building around 11.30pm.Moments later, half the wing collapsed, trapping many residents and labourers under the rubble.Over the next 15 hours, NDRF, fire brigade and Thane disaster response force personnel pulled out the bodies of Rakesh Paswan (25), Mukesh Paswan (30), Ashok Paswan (40), Krish Kumar (32), Ranjit Singh (45), Radheshyam Kushwaha (45), Siraj Rasul Sheikh (45), Shamim Ansari (32), Shyam Pal (40), and Santosh Pandey (42).Those injured, Abhay Yadav (26), Deepak Yadav (25) and Sangeeta Prajapati (36), were taken to a hospital. Some residents were rescued from the portion of the wing that remained standing.An NDRF officer said the building suffered a “pancake collapse”, in which one floor falls directly onto another.“The chances of survival in such collapses are extremely low. We deployed trained sniffer dogs to locate the victims.”Disaster management minister Girish Mahajan, who visited the site, said the repairs were carried out late at night to escape civic scrutiny.He directed the authorities to ensure that all dangerous buildings in Bhiwandi are vacated and appropriate action.Mehtab Ansari, a resident, told TOI that all flat owners had contributed around Rs 10,000 each for the repairs.Another resident, Komal Arvind Gupta, alleged that negligence during the work damaged the pillar.
Article Summary: An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed.

Article Title: Trump revokes 28,000 immigrant trucker licences: What it means for Indians
Article Text:
Trump administration targets migrant truck drivers

The administration of US President Donald Trump has cancelled the commercial driver's licences of more than 28,000 undocumented immigrants, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed on Tuesday.The administration is also launching a programme to replace the affected migrant truck drivers with US military veterans. At the end of last month, Trump announced the "Freedom Haul" initiative, aimed at replacing undocumented migrant truck drivers with US military veterans.In a recent press release, the US administration said it had coordinated with state authorities to revoke the commercial driver's licences (CDLs) of 24,000 non-citizens who, it said, did not meet English-language proficiency requirements.It also said officials had worked with states to cancel 28,000 commercial licences that it described as having been "illegally issued" and to shut down 9,500 driving schools that the administration alleged had helped unqualified drivers obtain licences and operate commercial vehicles on US roads.The US Department of Transportation began enforcing existing English-language proficiency requirements for commercial truck drivers last summer.aThe issue drew renewed attention following a fatal crash in Florida in August, when a truck driver allegedly made an illegal U-turn, killing three people. US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the Indian-origin driver involved in the crash should not have been issued a commercial driver's licence.“We are removing more and more dangerous foreign drivers off our roads every day and restoring the integrity of America’s trucking industry,” Duffy said. “Our new Freedom Haulers campaign will help build on these successes and get the word out that there’s never been a better time for America’s former service members to get behind the wheel of a big rig.”The Trump administration said audits carried out across all US states found numerous commercial driver's licences held by non-domiciled immigrants that remained valid after their work permits had expired or had been issued without proper verification of immigration or citizenship status.According to the US department of transportation, about 26,000 commercial drivers have since been removed from service for failing to meet English-language proficiency requirements, while nearly 30,000 commercial driver's licences were revoked after authorities determined they had been issued improperly.The federal government has also sought to withhold millions of dollars in highway funding from California and New York, accusing the states of failing to revoke additional licences. The funding dispute is now before the courts. Several other states, including Pennsylvania, Minnesota and North Carolina, have also been warned they could lose federal highway funding if they fail to comply with the administration's directives.Under the new rules, commercial driver's licences will be available only to immigrants holding valid H-2A, H-2B or E-2 visas. The H-2A visa is issued to temporary agricultural workers, the H-2B visa to temporary non-agricultural workers, while the E-2 visa is granted to foreign nationals who make substantial investments in a US business.According to administration figures, immigrants make up roughly 20 per cent of the US trucking workforce. However, non-domiciled commercial driver's licences issued to immigrants account for about 5 per cent of all commercial licences, representing approximately 200,000 drivers.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has cancelled the commercial driver's licences of more than 28,000 undocumented immigrants. The administration is also launching a programme to replace the affected migrant truck drivers with US military veterans. The issue drew renewed attention following a fatal crash in Florida in August, when a truck driver allegedly made an illegal U-turn.

Article Title: North Koreans told to eat dog meat soup to beat summer heat
Article Text:
North Korea’s state media recommends dog meat soup to combat summer heat as temperatures soar above 40°C across the peninsula.

North Korea’s state media has served up an unusual recipe for beating the summer heat: dog meat soup. The recommendation comes as a severe heatwave grips the Korean peninsula, with temperatures soaring above 40°C in parts of the region.According to the South China Morning Post, Rodong Sinmun, the newspaper of Kim Jong Un’s ruling Workers’ Party, published the advice on Sunday, as part of guidance on coping with the heatwave, which also included first-aid measures for heat-related illnesses.Speaking to the newspaper, a senior doctor at Pyongyang general hospital warned that “cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and hyperthyroidism can worsen due to heat exhaustion and heatstroke”.The paper recommended cooling foods such as watermelon, mung beans and cucumbers, alongside “highly nutritious foods” including dog meat soup, fish porridge and red bean porridge, reviving Pyongyang’s long-running promotion of the controversial dish, as a traditional health food.Locally known as dangogi guk, the dog meat soup remains relatively expensive and is beyond the reach of many ordinary North Koreans.“Dangogi is popular in the North, but it is a pricey food,” Ri Chol, a former North Korean diplomat, told This Week in Asia, according to the Post. “It is mostly consumed on hot summer days to help fend off heat exhaustion,” he said.Pyongyang has promoted dog meat for decades, including through speciality restaurants and annual cooking competitions designed to highlight the dish as part of the country’s culinary traditions.South Korea has moved to phase out the practice of eating dog meat entirely. A law passed in 2024 prohibits the breeding, slaughter, distribution and sale of dogs for human consumption. The ban is being implemented after a three-year transition period, which ends in February 2027. Once the grace period expires, those violating the law could face up to three years in prison or fines of up to 30 million South Korean won.North Korea has meanwhile been experiencing persistent heat. Since July 27, Pyongyang has recorded a series of tropical nights, with overnight temperatures remaining above 25 degrees Celsius.The Korean Central Broadcasting Station reported on Monday that a “sweltering heat advisory” would remain in place across much of the country through Sunday.Daytime temperatures are forecast to climb to between 33°C and 35°C in several areas, while relative humidity is expected to remain above 70 per cent.South Korea is also facing severe heat, with temperatures recently exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in parts of the southeast. The heat is expected to spread towards the Seoul metropolitan area.
Article Summary: Rodong Sinmun, the newspaper of Kim Jong Un’s ruling Workers’ Party, published the advice on Sunday, as part of guidance on coping with the heatwave. A senior doctor at Pyongyang general hospital warned that “cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and hyperthyroidism can worsen”.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district, died in the blast. He worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: Inspired by Hollywood series, Delhi man stages wife's murder as suicide
Article Text:
A Delhi man murdered his wife over property disputes and fled with significant cash. (File photo)

(With PTI inputs)





NEW DELHI: A 53-year-old Delhi man allegedly murdered his wife over a long-running property dispute and tried to mislead investigators using a crime strategy he claimed to have learnt from the Hollywood series 'The Staircase'.His plan, however, unravelled after police tracked him through CCTV footage and technical surveillance.The accused, Kamal Singh, was arrested near Mathura Railway Station following a multi-state manhunt by Shahdara police. During interrogation, he told investigators that he believed concealing the real murder weapon and planting another at the crime scene would help him evade arrest.The murder came to light on the night of July 30 when the couple's son returned to their Gagan Vihar home in Shahdara and found his mother, Komal Singh (50), lying in a pool of blood.According to police, a blood-stained pair of scissors had been placed in the victim's hand to make it appear that she had taken her own life."The victim's son immediately suspected foul play and alleged that his father had murdered his mother," a senior police officer said.During the investigation, police recovered a sword that they believe was the actual murder weapon. The accused had allegedly hidden it in a bag and attempted to dispose of it to destroy evidence.CCTV footage proved crucial in cracking the case. Investigators found that after the couple's two children left home that morning, only Kamal and his wife remained inside the house. The footage also allegedly captured the victim's screams before the accused was seen leaving with a bag containing the concealed weapon.Police said Singh had withdrawn around Rs 7 lakh from his bank accounts before fleeing. Technical surveillance traced his movements from Delhi towards Gorakhpur, where he allegedly planned to cross into Nepal. He later changed course and travelled towards Mathura, allegedly in an attempt to mislead investigators.He was eventually intercepted near Mathura Railway Station. Police recovered Rs 12.75 lakh in cash and a scooter allegedly used to flee after the murder.During questioning, Singh allegedly confessed that he had planned the killing in advance because of a prolonged family property dispute. He also admitted buying the scissors a few days before the murder to stage the crime scene."He said he was influenced by The Staircase and believed disposing of the real weapon while leaving another at the scene would derail the investigation. However, scientific evidence, CCTV analysis and technical surveillance exposed the carefully planned plot," the officer said.Further investigation, including forensic examination and additional recoveries, is underway.
Article Summary: A 53-year-old Delhi man allegedly murdered his wife over a long-running property dispute. Kamal Singh tried to mislead investigators using a crime strategy he claimed to have learnt from the Hollywood series 'The Staircase' His plan, however, unravelled after police tracked him through CCTV footage.

Article Title: Saurav Das alleges trespass at Delhi home after address surfaced online, complaint filed
Article Text:
YouTubers allegedly trespassed into CJP spokesperson Saurav Das's Delhi residence on Wednesday morning





NEW DELHI: Days after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das ’s house address and rent paid became a topic of discussion on social media, some YouTubers allegedly tried to enter his house Wednesday morning.Das, who is in Maharashtra for a meeting with other CJP functionaries, tagged Delhi Police in a post on X, “Certain YouTubers and media channels have broken into my house and are showing the visuals from inside. It’s not just an invasion of my privacy but also a grave security threat for me and my family. If anti-social elements attack me at my residence as a result of this, these YouTubers and their troll handlers who are coordinating this will be directly responsible.”He also said that 15–20 people reached his house Wednesday morning while others had been camping outside since Tuesday evening.Das, through his lawyer, filed a complaint with the Greater Kailash police station SHO, Wednesday evening.“Over the past several days, and continuing till date, various unknown persons claiming to be YouTubers/journalists/content creators and media personnel have been repeatedly assembling outside, and unlawfully entering, the residential premises of the complainant (Das)...without any authority, permission or consent... These persons have not merely gathered outside the premises but have deliberately trespassed into the residence,” the complaint said.The complaint urged police to register an FIR for trespass and intimidation and said Das’s address had been disclosed by two social media handles, “encouraging members of the public to visit the premises”.Police said they had received the complaint and were investigating the matter.“Local beat officers have been deployed in the vicinity and are keeping a watch to prevent any untoward situation,” police officials said.Ashutosh Ranka, CJP spokesperson told reporters in Maharashtra that Das’s family members were at home when the incident occurred.“We will not get scared... This is their classic playbook, where they first try to crush you and suppress a movement. When they were not able to do that, they slung mud at us. When people rejected this, they tried to spread violence... A hate campaign is being run against him (Das)... By doing these things, you are losing whatever respect you had,” Ranka said.
Article Summary: YouTubers allegedly trespassed into CJP spokesperson Saurav Das's Delhi residence on Wednesday morning. Das is in Maharashtra for a meeting with other CJP functionaries. He filed a complaint with the Greater Kailash police station SHO, Wednesday evening.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Bombay high court asks Mumbai Police why no FIR was filed on murder complaint
Article Text:
Aadvocate Nilesh Ojha claimed the court had raised serious concerns over the police investigation.





MUMBAI: Advocate Nilesh Ojha, representing Disha Salian's father Satish Salian has said the Bombay high court on Thursday questioned the Mumbai Police over its decision not to register an FIR in the death of celebrity manager Disha Salian, despite her family's allegations of murder, during the hearing of a petition seeking a fresh investigation into the 2020 case.Ojha said, a division bench of Justice Bharti Dangre and Justice Manjusha Deshpande sought an explanation from the police on why only an Accidental Death Report (ADR) was registered when Disha's father, Satish Salian, had lodged a complaint alleging gang rape and murder.The court also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and the ADR had not been provided to the family even five years after her death.Aadvocate Nilesh Ojha claimed the court had raised serious concerns over the police investigation."The court severely reprimanded the police. It clearly stated that the nature of the investigation into the accidental death, regardless of its findings, was not the core issue. When the girl's father expressed doubts about the police's version and lodged a complaint alleging gang rape and murder, what prevented the police from registering an FIR and conducting an investigation? Why was this not done? The court posed this direct question," he said.Ojha further alleged that the bench found the police's theory that Disha died by suicide after falling from the 14th floor inconsistent with the material placed before it."The court examined the evidence on record. It rejected the police's claim that she had fallen from the 14th floor and committed suicide, as this theory was inconsistent with the evidence and lacked credibility. The court noted the condition of the body seen in photographs taken during the funeral and observed that it appeared intact despite the alleged fall. We also pointed out that eyewitnesses had stated she had not sustained visible injuries," he claimed.During the hearing, the bench directed the petitioner to file a chronological list of events and circumstances that, according to the family, disclose a cognisable offence.The respondents, including the Maharashtra government through the Mumbai Police, have been asked to respond to those submissions.Satish Salian has approached the high court seeking a fresh probe into his daughter's death, alleging foul play and seeking the interrogation of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray.The petition challenges the earlier conclusion that Disha Salian's death was accidental and seeks a fresh investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident.Earlier, the Mumbai Police told the high court that the findings of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) were consistent with the conclusions of the original investigation, which ruled out foul play in the death of the 28-year-old celebrity manager in 2020.The police, however, said the SIT was continuing to examine all possible angles.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: The Bombay high court on Thursday questioned the Mumbai Police over its decision not to register an FIR in the death of Disha Salian. A division bench of Justice Bharti Dangre and Justice Manjusha Deshpande sought an explanation from the police on why only an Accidental Death Report (ADR) was registered.

Article Title: Mahayuti rift: BJP unhappy with Shiv Sena's Sanjay Shirsat visiting Abhijit Dipke kin
Article Text:
The BJP is upset with Eknath Shinde's Shiv Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat's family visit.





MUMBAI: The BJP is upset with Eknath Shinde's Shiv Sena over its minister Sanjay Shirsat visiting Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke's family and meeting them in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.After the BJP expressed displeasure over Shirsat's meeting the Dipkes, saying it indicated his backing for Dipke, Shinde is said to have given Shirsat a dressing down on Tuesday when the state cabinet meeting was conducted.Speaking on reports that he could be dropped from the cabinet, Shirsat denied there was any reshuffle in the offing.The BJP said it was not right for a Mahayuti party's minister to meet Dipke's parents and praise him.BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Shinde must take stern action against such people. "Ultimately it is their party's decision. How their netas must behave, this is up to Eknath Shinde. Eknath Shinde has spoken on this. While working in Mahayuti this kind of conduct is not right and I'm sure Eknath Shinde will take appropriate action," Bawankule said.BJP functionaries said the BJP's top leadership had taken note of Shirsat's visit to Dipke's residence and meeting with his family and they too had expressed their displeasure.Last month, Shirsat met Dipke's parents and promised their son would get security cover, a day after the CJP agitation was called off following Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
Article Summary: The BJP is upset with Eknath Shinde's Shiv Sena over its minister Sanjay Shirsat visiting Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke's family and meeting them in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The BJP said it was not right for a Mahayuti party's minister to meet Dipke’s parents and praise him.

Article Title: Mumbai Police Arrest Man in Goa for 2017 Andheri Scrap Dealer Murder
Article Text:
The accused kept changing his name after he fled to Karnataka and later relocated to Goa in 2020





Mumbai: The MIDC police arrested a man from Goa who was wanted in the murder of a scrap dealer in Andheri nine years ago. Six other accused in the case are already out on bail. The police found that Mehtab Khan (46) was working with a scrap dealer in Goa.Khan kept changing his name after he fled to Karnataka and later relocated to Goa in 2020. “The MIDC police team nabbed Khan after they gathered information from a website of scrapdealers in Goa that get govt tenders. Accordingly, the team caught him on August 4,” DCP Datta NalawadeAssistant inspector Pravin Rakshe said Khan aided six others, arrested in 2017, to kill the victim as he tipped the Nashik police about person who was brother to one of the six arrested accused.MIDC police senior inspector Ghanshyam Nair said first picked Khan’s younger brother, thinking that he was the one who had committed the murder. But during questioning, he told the police that he was not the suspect. It was his elder brother who resembled him, he told the police.Inspector Sunil Karande said Khan, along with six others, allegedly bludgeoned Wasimullah Mohsin Shaikh (41) to death using iron rods on Feb 3, 2017, after inviting him for lunch.
Article Summary: Mehtab Khan (46) was working with a scrap dealer in Goa. Khan, along with six others, allegedly bludgeoned Wasimullah Mohsin Shaikh to death using iron rods on Feb 3, 2017. Khan kept changing his name after he fled to Karnataka and later relocated to Goa in 2020.
